acceptances.table_meaning: Stores individual acceptance records (e.g., a user or entity accepting a request, terms, or offer), each identified by a unique ID.

columns.id: Primary key, unique identifier for each acceptance record (typically an auto‑increment integer).

administrator_conference.table_meaning: A junction table that links administrators to the conferences they manage or are associated with, representing a many‑to‑many relationship between administrators and conferences.

columns.aid: Foreign key referencing the unique identifier of an administrator (e.g., user or staff ID).
columns.cid: Foreign key referencing the unique identifier of a conference (e.g., event or meeting ID).

administrators.table_meaning: Stores information about system administrators and whether each has the authority to accept submitted papers.

columns.id: Unique identifier for each administrator (primary key).
columns.accept_paper: Boolean flag (or similar) indicating if the administrator is permitted to accept/review submitted papers.

associated_chairs.table_meaning: Stores records that represent chairs (e.g., committee or conference chairs) that are linked or associated with other entities in the system.

columns.id: Primary key uniquely identifying each associated chair record.

author_not_reviewers.table_meaning: Stores a list of author identifiers that are excluded from acting as reviewers.

columns.id: Primary key for the record, typically referencing an author ID that should not be assigned reviewer duties.

authors.table_meaning: Stores a list of unique author identifiers, representing individual authors in the system.

columns.id: Primary key for the author; a unique integer (or string) that identifies each author.

bids.table_meaning: Stores individual bids submitted in an auction or procurement process, including any adjustments made to the original amount.

columns.id: Unique identifier for each bid record (primary key).
columns.adjusted: Flag or value indicating whether the bid amount has been modified after the initial submission.
columns.bid: The monetary value of the bid (original or current).

chairmans.table_meaning: Stores unique identifiers for individuals who serve or have served as chairmen (e.g., board chairs) in the organization.

columns.id: Primary key; a unique identifier for each chairman record.

co_author_paper.table_meaning: A junction table that records which co‑authors (identified by cid) have contributed to which papers (identified by pid), representing a many‑to‑many relationship between authors and papers.

columns.cid: Identifier for a co‑author (author ID) in the system.
columns.pid: Identifier for a paper (paper ID) in the system.

co_authors.table_meaning: Stores the identifiers of authors who are designated as co‑authors, typically referencing a primary authors table.

columns.id: Unique identifier for the co‑author; serves as a foreign key linking to the main authors table.

conf_members.table_meaning: Stores the identifiers of members that belong to a particular conference or configuration group.

columns.id: Unique identifier of a member (likely a foreign key referencing a member record).

conference_administrator.table_meaning: Associative table linking conferences to their administrators, defining which administrator manages each conference.

columns.cid: Identifier of the conference (foreign key to the conferences table).
columns.aid: Identifier of the administrator (foreign key to the administrators table).

conference_chairs.table_meaning: Stores records for individuals who serve as chairs of conferences, typically linking to a person or user entity.

columns.id: Primary key identifier for each conference chair record.

conference_members.table_meaning: A linking (junction) table that records which members are registered for or belong to each conference, representing a many‑to‑many relationship between conferences and members.

columns.conference: The identifier (likely a foreign key) of a conference.
columns.conference_member: The identifier (likely a foreign key) of a member who is associated with the conference.

conferences.table_meaning: Stores basic information about academic or professional conferences, including identifiers, names, dates, and related web resources.

columns.id: Unique identifier for each conference record (primary key).
columns.site_url: Web address of the conference's official website.
columns.accepts_hardcopy_submissions: Flag indicating whether the conference accepts physical (paper) submissions (e.g., true/false or null if unknown).
columns.logo_url: Link to an image file containing the conference's logo.
columns.date: Date on which the conference takes place (typically the start date).
columns.name: Short name or acronym of the conference (e.g., SIGXYZ, XSWC).
columns.reviews_per_paper: Number of peer reviews each submitted paper is expected to receive (null if not recorded).

decisions.table_meaning: Stores individual decision records, each representing a choice or action taken within the application.

columns.id: Unique identifier (primary key) for each decision entry.

details_entered.table_meaning: Stores a relationship between two entities, recording that a detail identified by one ID has been entered for the entity identified by the other ID.

columns.cid: Identifier of the primary entity (e.g., customer, case, content) for which a detail was entered.
columns.aid: Identifier of the associated detail or secondary entity (e.g., address, attribute, author) that was entered.

documents.table_meaning: Stores a list of documents, each identified by a unique document ID.

columns.id: A unique identifier (primary key) for each document, represented as a string.

enable_virtual_meeting.table_meaning: Associates a primary entity (such as an account, user, or appointment) with a specific meeting or conference to indicate that virtual meeting functionality is enabled for that pairing.

columns.aid: Identifier of the primary entity (e.g., account ID, user ID, or appointment ID).
columns.cid: Identifier of the meeting, conference, or client for which virtual meeting is permitted.

external_reviewers.table_meaning: Stores records of reviewers who are external to the organization and the internal reviewer who assigned them to a review task.

columns.id: Primary key that uniquely identifies each external reviewer entry.
columns.assigned_by_reviewer: Reference (typically a foreign key) to the internal reviewer who assigned this external reviewer.

finalize_paper_assignment.table_meaning: Stores the finalized mapping of papers to their assigned reviewers (or committees) after the assignment process is locked.

columns.aid: Unique identifier for each assignment record (Assignment ID).
columns.cid: Identifier of the paper (or conference) that is being assigned (Paper/Conference ID).

hardcopy_mailing_manifests_p.table_meaning: Stores the association between a mailing campaign and the physical addresses that are included in its hard‑copy mailing manifest.

columns.cid: Identifier of the mailing campaign (e.g., campaign ID).
columns.aid: Identifier of the address or recipient record to be mailed (e.g., address ID).

mark_conflict_interests.table_meaning: Records which conference members have a declared conflict of interest with which submitted papers, used to prevent them from reviewing those papers.

columns.conference_member: Identifier (e.g., user ID or name) of the conference participant (reviewer, committee member, etc.) who has a conflict.
columns.paper: Identifier (e.g., paper ID or title) of the submitted paper that the conference member is conflicted with.

meta_reviewers.table_meaning: Stores the unique identifiers of meta reviewers (reviewers who evaluate other reviewers) in the system.

columns.id: Primary key; unique identifier for each meta reviewer, typically referencing a user record.

meta_reviews.table_meaning: Stores metadata or summary information about individual reviews, with each row representing a distinct meta review record.

columns.id: Primary key identifier for the meta review entry.

paper_abstracts.table_meaning: Stores a unique identifier for each paper abstract, linking to the full abstract text stored elsewhere or in a related table.

columns.id: Primary key (or foreign key) that uniquely identifies a paper abstract record.

paper_assignment_tools_run.table_meaning: Tracks each execution of the paper‑assignment tool for a conference, linking a conference to a specific assignment run.

columns.cid: Identifier of the conference (or call for papers) the assignment run belongs to.
columns.aid: Identifier of the specific assignment tool run (e.g., a particular execution of the reviewer‑paper matching algorithm).

paper_author.table_meaning: A junction table that records which authors contributed to which papers, representing a many-to-many relationship between papers and authors.

columns.aid: Foreign key referencing the unique identifier of an author in the authors table.
columns.pid: Foreign key referencing the unique identifier of a paper in the papers table.

paper_full_versions.table_meaning: Stores identifiers of papers that have a complete/full version available, typically referencing entries in a main papers table.

columns.id: Primary key or foreign key referencing the unique identifier of a paper that has a full version.

paper_reviewer.table_meaning: Maps each paper to the reviewers assigned to evaluate it, representing a many‑to‑many relationship between papers and reviewers.

columns.pid: Identifier of the paper (foreign key to a papers table).
columns.rid: Identifier of the reviewer (foreign key to a reviewers table).

paper_subject_area.table_meaning: A junction table linking research papers to their subject areas, representing a many‑to‑many relationship between papers and topics.

columns.pid: Foreign key referencing the unique identifier of a paper in the papers table.
columns.sid: Foreign key referencing the unique identifier of a subject area in the subject_areas table.

papers.table_meaning: Tracks submissions (papers) to a conference or journal, recording their identifiers, author, title, and the review/decision status.

columns.id: Internal primary‑key for the record in this table.
columns.paper_id: External or public identifier for the submitted paper (e.g., submission number).
columns.rejected: Boolean flag (or nullable) indicating whether the paper was rejected.
columns.read_by_meta_reviewer: Boolean flag (or nullable) showing if a meta‑reviewer has opened/read the submission.
columns.author: Identifier (likely a user or author ID) of the person who submitted the paper.
columns.title: The title of the submitted paper.
columns.decision: Text or code representing the final decision (e.g., "accept", "reject", "revise").
columns.accepted: Boolean flag (or nullable) indicating whether the paper was accepted.

pc_members.table_meaning: Stores information about program committee (PC) members for a conference or journal management system, tracking each member's identity and review capacity.

columns.id: Unique identifier for the PC member (e.g., user or reviewer ID).
columns.max_papers: The maximum number of papers the member is allowed to review or be assigned.
columns.added: Timestamp (or date) indicating when the member was added to the PC list.

person_document.table_meaning: A junction table that records which documents are associated with which persons, representing a many‑to‑many relationship between people and documents.

columns.pid: Foreign key referencing the primary key of the person table; identifies the person.
columns.did: Foreign key referencing the primary key of the document table; identifies the document.

persons.table_meaning: The table stores basic contact information for individual persons, likely members or employees of an organization.

columns.id: A unique identifier for each person, typically used as the primary key.
columns.name: The full name of the person.
columns.email: The person's email address, used for communication.

preferences.table_meaning: Stores individual preference records, each uniquely identified by an ID, likely used to reference specific user or system preferences.

columns.id: Primary key identifier for each preference entry, typically an auto-increment integer.

program_committee_chair_review.table_meaning: Associative table linking a program (e.g., a paper or submission) to the review performed by the program committee chair.

columns.pid: Identifier of the program, paper, or submission.
columns.rid: Identifier of the review record created by the program committee chair.

program_committee_chairs.table_meaning: Contains the identifiers of people who act as chairs of program committees, linking each chair to program committee records stored in other tables.

columns.id: Unique identifier (usually a foreign key) for a person or user who serves as a program committee chair.

program_committee_members.table_meaning: Maps each program committee to the individuals who serve as its members, representing a many‑to‑many relationship between committees and members.

columns.program_committee: Identifier (likely a foreign key) of a specific program committee.
columns.program_committee_member: Identifier (likely a foreign key) of a person or entity that is a member of the referenced program committee.

program_committees.table_meaning: Stores distinct program committee groups, typically identified by conference/workshop acronym and year, used to associate reviewers, papers, or other data with a specific committee.

columns.id: Unique numeric identifier (primary key) for each program committee record.
columns.label: Descriptive name of the committee, usually combining the conference/workshop acronym and the year (e.g., "XSWC 2015 Program Committee").

read_by_reviewer.table_meaning: Tracks which reviewers have read which papers, indicating a read status for each reviewer-paper pair.

columns.pid: Identifier of the paper (or submission) that may have been read.
columns.rid: Identifier of the reviewer who has read the paper.

rejections.table_meaning: Stores a list of rejection records, typically used to reference items (e.g., applications, orders, or transactions) that have been denied or marked as invalid.

columns.id: Primary key that uniquely identifies each rejection entry.

reviewer_administrator.table_meaning: Associative table linking reviewers to administrators, indicating which administrator is assigned to which reviewer.

columns.aid: Foreign key referencing the unique identifier of an administrator.
columns.rid: Foreign key referencing the unique identifier of a reviewer.

reviewers.table_meaning: Stores the unique identifiers of individuals who act as reviewers in a review or approval workflow.

columns.id: A primary key that uniquely identifies each reviewer.

reviews.table_meaning: Stores individual peer‑review comments for academic papers, linking each review to a unique identifier and the reviewer who wrote it.

columns.id: Primary key for the review record (unique identifier for each review).
columns.written: Identifier of the reviewer (foreign key to a users/reviewers table).
columns.comment: The full text of the review, including references to the paper being evaluated.

set_max_papers.table_meaning: Maps which administrators are authorized to set the maximum number of papers for each program committee member.

columns.administrator: Identifier (e.g., user ID) of the administrator who can configure paper limits.
columns.program_committee_member: Identifier (e.g., user ID) of the program committee member whose paper limit can be set.

subject_areas.table_meaning: Stores unique identifiers for each subject area, used as a reference in other tables to categorize content by academic or topical subject.

columns.id: Primary key that uniquely identifies a subject area.

users.table_meaning: Stores a list of user accounts, each identified by a unique identifier.

columns.id: A unique identifier (primary key) for each user.
